references.text: The same ritual of laying hands on the head of the sacrificial animal is described for the burnt offering, symbolizing identification with the sacrifice.
Parallel text concerning the laying on of hands and slaughter of a peace offering from cattle, with the same ritual actions.
The same ritual is repeated for the goat offering, involving laying on of hands, slaughter, and sprinkling of blood.
Laying of hands on the head of the sin offering before slaughter, following the same ritual pattern.
Sprinkling of blood around the altar by Aaron's sons, the same priestly action as in the peace offering ritual.
Laying of hands on the sin offering during the consecration of priests, fundamental to the sacrificial ritual.
The blood is sprinkled around the altar, the same action performed by the priests.
Hebrews explains that almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law, and points to the significance of the sprinkling of blood.
Clarifies the principle that sacrificial blood must always be handled by the priesthood at the altar to make atonement, even though the location varies.
Shows the historical fulfillment of the instructions during the consecration of the priesthood, where the rituals were followed exactly.
Highlights the common necessity of laying on of hands and slaughter at the entrance for all types of offerings before blood handling begins.
Creates a theological contrast between the blood handling of the sin offering (pouring out) and the complete sprinkling of the peace offering.
